reader.decision: Do both, in order. Make charge_renewals idempotent first (renewal_charges check per subscription for today, plus a Payrail idempotency key only if Payrail is confirmed to accept one). Then apply the slot-key fix to scheduler/clock.py and scheduler/loop.py. Hold the refund reconciliation until the database is available.
reader.decision_reason: The double charge moved money, and the slot key is held only in memory, so a restart inside the repeated hour loses it. The message itself says idempotency should be primary when money safety matters more. The slot key is still worth having because it also stops the repeated send_dunning emails, which idempotency does not.

reconstruction.problem: On 25 October the Berlin clock showed 02:30 twice because DST ended. The cron matched both times. The only repeat guard, MIN_GAP_SECONDS = 60 measured in UTC, allowed the second run because 3600 s had passed. charge_renewals selects every subscription with renews_on <= today and does not mark them as charged, so the second run found the same 212 rows and charged them again. send_dunning also repeated and sent the same 41 emails.
reconstruction.what_breaks: 212 subscribers were charged twice and 41 dunning emails were sent twice. settle_renewals then settled 424 rows. No refund list exists per KB-519.
reconstruction.fix: Slot key: in scheduler/clock.py, delete the MIN_GAP_SECONDS check and skip a job when last_fired[job.name] equals (local.date(), local.hour, local.minute). In scheduler/loop.py, store that tuple in last_fired instead of now_utc, with local computed before due_jobs. Alternative: make charge_renewals idempotent by skipping subscriptions that already have a renewal_charges row for today and sending a per-subscription key to Payrail. Cleanup: diff renewal_charges rows with charged_on = '2026-10-25' (expected two per subscription) against Payrail dashboard refunds.
reconstruction.cost: The slot key keeps last_fired in memory, so a restart inside the repeated hour loses the guard, and the spring-forward gap still skips a job once a year. The idempotent alternative does not fix send_dunning, and it is not stated whether Payrail accepts an idempotency key. The refund reconciliation has not been run because the database is not in the directory.

follow_up_questions: Does Payrail accept an idempotency key on charge requests? If not, the renewal_charges check must be the only guard.
Can I get read access to the database and the Payrail dashboard to run the refund reconciliation?
